title: f32->f16 bit conversion rounds half-up and double-rounds subnormals
source_subject: fix: Manual float16 conversions to extend platform support (#2773)
description: toHalfBits() reverted to its pre-fix form: normalised numbers use "mant + 0x1000" (round half up) instead of round-to-nearest-even; subnormals shift first and round afterwards. Wrong 1-ulp f16 results for tie / subnormal inputs in f16() casts folded at comptime, std.bitcast to f16, pack2x16float on the CPU and the no-eval writer fallback.
notes: Reached only via CPU-side conversions (the compiled writer uses DataView.setFloat16, so ordinary f16 buffer writes are NOT affected). No GPU suite found that folds an f16 literal on a tie value -> expected unreachable by suites.
backend_note: f16 only: SwiftShader has no shader-f16; Lavapipe/Metal do
adapted_from_fix: full reversal of the toHalfBits hunks

title: Perlin dynamic cache never clears its dirty flag
source_subject: fix: Reset dirty flag in Perlin noise dynamic caches (#3159)
description: Removed "dirty = false" after re-creating the memory buffer in bindings getter: once the size was changed every later read of .bindings destroys and regenerates the gradient buffer (a compute dispatch) again.
notes: Output values stay identical (same gradients regenerated) -> detection needs resource-churn / perf / validation (use of a destroyed buffer). Deliberately a near-equivalent, host-only mutant.

title: tgpu.unroll over a range ending at 0 is dropped
source_subject: fix: tgpu.unroll removing ranges ending at zero (#3040)
description: Unroll codegen again returns an empty block when range.end === 0 (checked before the elements are computed), so tgpu.unroll(std.range(-2, 0)) or std.range(3, 0, -1) silently unrolls zero iterations.
notes: Unrolled std.range(a, 0) is absent from all suites and from the docs examples (checked by grep): unreachable, host/codegen only. Mocked tests cover it (wgslGenerator range(3,0,-1)).
adapted_from_fix: exact (code moved: knownEnd instead of range.end.value)

title: withIndexBuffer ignores the element-count size argument
description: For the TgpuBuffer overload sizeBytes is computed from the 4th (GPUBuffer-only) parameter instead of the 3rd, so withIndexBuffer(buf, offsetElements, sizeElements) drops sizeElements and binds the whole tail of the buffer.
notes: Only observable when an offset/size is passed; no docs example does. Renders more indices than requested.

title: isCloseTo for vectors emits "(lhs - lhs) + precision" (lhs evaluated twice)
description: Reverted the WGSL emitted for std.isCloseTo(vecA, vecB, p) to "all(abs(a - b) <= (a - a) + p)". Numerically identical for finite a, but duplicates (and re-evaluates) the lhs expression and yields NaN for infinite lhs.
notes: Pure generated-text difference with equal GPU values for all finite inputs: the canonical "mocks see it, GPUs cannot" case. tgsl-parsing-test calls isCloseTo with constant vectors; whether it hits codegen or the CPU impl depends on const folding.
adapted_from_fix: exact (unused coerceToSnippet import left in place)

title: CPU std.saturate throws for float vectors
source_subject: fix: CPU implementation of saturate for float vectors (#3183)
description: cpuSaturate() reverted: vectors throw MissingCpuImplError. During shader comptime folding that error is swallowed and the codegen path is used, so only JS-side calls std.saturate(vec3f(...)) are affected.
notes: GPU values unaffected (dualImpl falls back to codegen on MissingCpuImplError). vector-fns runtime-matrix evaluates saturate on vec2f..vec4f on the CPU, but accepts "not implemented yet" throws, so the test still passes - only the recorded statistics change. Included as a GPU-blind mutant.

title: Integer-valued literals >= 2^63 typed as abstractInt (FLT_MAX in oklab)
description: Removed the "value >= 2**63 -> abstractFloat" guard in numericLiteralToSnippet: huge integer-valued JS numbers such as 3.40282346e38 (FLT_MAX in @typegpu/color oklab gamut mapping) are typed abstractInt instead of abstractFloat.
notes: Static analysis: emitted literal text is the same ("3.40282346e+38"); only the TypeGPU type differs, so it can change conversions/overloads in integer contexts but probably not the oklab output. Treat as likely-equivalent; could not be run (read-only, no installs).
adapted_from_fix: only the generationHelpers hunk (oklab FLT_MAX hunk already merged in HEAD form)

title: Compiled writer leaves mat3x3f column padding unwritten
description: buildWriter() for matrices reverted to write only matSize*matSize floats (skipping the padding float of each mat3x3f column) instead of zeroing the padding. Stale bytes survive in the padding of a re-used host buffer.
notes: Bytes differ only in padding; shaders cannot observe them -> invisible to every GPU suite; visible to byte-level mocked tests (arrayBufferIO "overrides all values when handling mat3x3f").
adapted_from_fix: compiledIO.ts hunk only (dataIO.ts no-eval fallback hunk not reverted)

title: Buffer allocations/transfers no longer padded to a multiple of 4 bytes
source_subject: fix: Pad buffer allocations and transfers to a multiple of 4 bytes (#3155)
description: physicalSizeOf() returns sizeOf(schema) again, so buffers whose logical size is not a multiple of 4 (d.f16, d.vec3h, arrayOf(d.u16, odd)) are created with an invalid size for mappedAtCreation / copyBufferToBuffer / writeBuffer.
notes: Every f16 createMutable (size 2 or 6) fails WebGPU validation on f16-capable backends (Lavapipe, Metal); on SwiftShader (no f16) those tests are skipped, so this is a backend-differentiating mutant. Also hits odd-length u16 arrays (docs examples with u16 index buffers of odd length).
backend_note: caught only where shader-f16 exists (Lavapipe yes, SwiftShader no)
adapted_from_fix: reverts only the physicalSizeOf() rounding (the aligned-write checks stay)

title: Non-finite comptime values are no longer rejected (Finite Math Assumption)
description: Removed the isFinite guards from the u32/i32/f32/f16 casts and from numericLiteral(): comptime-folded Infinity/NaN (e.g. 1/0) is emitted into WGSL as "Infinityf"/"NaNf" and fails shader compilation instead of raising TypeGPU's explicit error.
notes: Behaviour differs only when a suite const-folds a non-finite value; error text changes from a TypeGPU error to a Dawn/WGSL compile error. Detected only if the suite records error messages/outcome classes.
adapted_from_fix: generator guard + cast guards (bool cast guard kept)

title: Auto vertex output does not receive fragment-determined varying locations
source_subject: fix: Pass locations to auto vertex out (#3174)
description: AutoVertexFn builds its output AutoStruct with undefined locations instead of the matched-up `locations`, so shell-less vertex outputs ignore custom @location()s declared on the fragment input.
expected_reachable_by: docs:*shell-less vertex+fragment pairs with explicit d.location (not identified)
notes: Only matters when a fragment input declares non-default locations paired with an auto vertex function; otherwise auto-numbering coincides. Symptom is a render-pipeline link mismatch/validation error or swapped varyings.

title: withLocations treats location 0 as "no location"
description: Truthiness check "if (locations[key])" instead of "!== undefined": a varying whose matched-up location is 0 is re-numbered by the free-slot allocator (which now skips reserved 0), giving it location 1 and colliding/mismatching with the other stage.
expected_reachable_by: docs:*shell-less pairs whose fragment pins location 0 (not identified)
notes: ADAPTED: HEAD also reserves Object.values(locations) in usedCustomLocations, so re-introducing the old falsy test now mis-numbers location 0 instead of being benign as in the original pre-fix code. Rarely exercised.

title: Global identifier resolved inside a nested call can capture a caller-local name
source_subject: fix: Global identifier inside nested function call (#2789)
description: isIdentifierTaken() only checks the current function's block scopes again (ignores the call stack for scope="global"), so a global resolved for the first time inside a nested function can receive the same generated name as a local of the calling function.
expected_reachable_by: docs:*examples with nested helper calls and local/global name collisions (not identified)
notes: Wrong-variable capture is possible but needs a collision between a caller local and a not-yet-emitted global name; unlikely in the small suites. When it triggers the result is a wrong value or a WGSL redeclaration error.
adapted_from_fix: behaviourally equivalent reversal inside isIdentifierTaken (helper left unused)

title: Implicit conversion i32/u32 <-> abstractFloat picks i32/u32 (truncates the float)
source_subject: fix: Choose `f32` when trying to find a type common with `abstractFloat` and `i32` (or `u32`) (#2396)
description: Removed the rule that casts i32/u32 to f32 when unified with an abstract float and restored the old abstractFloat->i32 (rank 1) / ->u32 (rank 2) conversions: expressions like i32Var * 0.5 or select(i32Var, 2.5, c) are evaluated in integer arithmetic.
expected_reachable_by: docs:*examples mixing integer variables with fractional literals
notes: Silent precision loss: the float literal is truncated to an integer. Reached only where a suite mixes a typed integer with a fractional JS literal inside a use-gpu function; mul-paths/new-findings already records related "v * 1.5 emitted as v * 1i" observations (vector path), so rows may shift there. Low-confidence reach.

title: hasIndexBuffer is a constant false field
description: The getter derived from priors.indexBuffer was replaced by a readonly field initialised to false, so pipelines created with withIndexBuffer still report hasIndexBuffer === false.
notes: Pure introspection flag, not used internally; GPU output unchanged. Expected unreachable.

title: Piping a configuration duplicates its bindings
source_subject: fix: Keep each binding once when piping a configuration (#3180)
description: ConfigurableImpl.pipe() concatenates this.bindings with transform(this).bindings (which already include them), so every slot binding appears twice.
notes: Later bindings of the same slot override earlier ones with identical values -> outputs equal; observable only through binding counts. Near-equivalent.

title: Generated identifiers may shadow WGSL template enumerants (read, write, uniform, rgba8unorm...)
source_subject: fix: Keep generated identifiers off the template-parameter enumerants (#3151)
description: templateEnumerants removed from takenGlobalIdentifiers: a user function/variable called e.g. `read` or `uniform` can be emitted verbatim and shadow the enumerant used in var<storage, read_write> / texture_storage_2d<rgba8unorm, write> templates.
notes: Needs a TypeGPU-resolved declaration with an enumerant name; none of the GPU suites define one. Symptom would be a WGSL compile error.

title: Unary minus on u32 no longer rejected by TypeGPU
description: The u32 check in std.neg's signature was removed, so -u32Var is emitted as WGSL "-(x)" on an unsigned value and is rejected only by the WGSL compiler.
notes: inv:scalar-int/scalar-contract.test.ts asserts exactly this error ("std.neg(u32) is rejected by TypeGPU at resolve time (#3118)"); host-side tgpu.resolve, no GPU needed. ported neg tests skip the CPU-only signature checks, so they do not see it.

title: Compiled writer uses unpadded element stride for arrays of vec3
description: In the compiled writer an array element stride is sizeOf(elementType) instead of roundUp(sizeOf, alignment): arrays of vec3f/vec3i/vec3u/vec3h written from JS arrays land at 12-byte (6 for vec3h) strides while WGSL reads 16-byte strides.
notes: Layout corruption only for arrays of vec3 written element-wise (typed-array inputs take the memcpy path). The 13 example tests and investigation suites only use standalone vec3 values, so likely unreachable by them.

title: Struct size loses trailing padding
description: computeMLOfStruct returns the unrounded size (no roundUp to struct alignment): standalone buffers of structs with tail padding are too small (binding-size validation error) and nested structs shift the following members.
expected_reachable_by: docs:*most examples with uniform/storage structs mixing vec/mat and scalars
notes: Structs without tail padding (all-u32 structs of bitonic-sort/matrix-next, MatrixStruct of matrix-multiplication: 152 bytes, align 8) are unaffected; structs such as log-test's ComplexStruct (20 bytes, align 16) are. Loud (validation) on every backend that checks min binding size.

title: vec3<f16> alignment 4 instead of 8
description: knownAlignmentMap.vec3h = 4: structs/arrays containing vec3h get member offsets/strides that differ from WGSL (align 8).
notes: Only matters for vec3h inside structs/arrays; suites use standalone vec3h values (no effect). f16-only.
backend_note: f16 only: SwiftShader cannot run it

title: mat3x3f columns written packed (36 bytes) by the compiled writer
description: wgslElementStride = matSize for matrices: mat3x3f columns are written at 12-byte pitch while WGSL expects 16-byte column pitch.
notes: Any GPU test that uploads a mat3x3f from a JS value and uses it in a shader sees shifted columns.

title: Compiled writer transposes matrices given as mat objects
description: For MatImpl inputs the writer reads columns[row].component[col] instead of columns[col].component[row] (row-/column-major mix-up). Typed-array and plain-array inputs are unaffected.
notes: Invisible for symmetric matrices (identity, scalings); any asymmetric matrix upload flips results.

title: std.mix emits mix(b, a, t)
description: Generated WGSL swaps the first two arguments of mix (argument-order bug).
notes: Result is 1 - t weighted; identical for t = 0.5 or a == b, so very subtle for symmetric tests, loud for t in {0,1}.

title: std.faceForward emits faceForward(e1, e3, e2)
description: Generated WGSL swaps the 2nd and 3rd arguments of faceForward.
notes: No mocked test mentions faceForward (grep over typegpu tests and docs snapshots). No CPU implementation, so only the GPU path exists.

title: std.countLeadingZeros emits countTrailingZeros
description: Copy-paste bug in codegen: countLeadingZeros(x) is emitted as countTrailingZeros(x).
notes: No CPU implementation exists (string normalImpl) and no mocked test mentions countLeadingZeros, so only a real GPU run can see it.

title: std.extractBits emits (offset, count) swapped
description: Generated WGSL calls extractBits(e, count, offset).
notes: Equal result when offset == count; no CPU implementation; no mocked test mentions extractBits.

title: CPU/comptime smoothstep has no clamp
description: smoothstepScalar drops clampScalar(...,0,1): comptime-folded smoothstep(e0, e1, x) returns t*t*(3-2t) for x outside [e0,e1] (values > 1 or < 0).
notes: Only the CPU implementation changes: seen when arguments are comptime-known (folded into the shader as a constant) or when the CPU impl is compared with an oracle.

title: CPU/comptime mod uses floored modulo
description: The CPU implementation of std.mod uses ((a % b) + b) % b: differs from WGSL/truncated semantics for negative operands (and for floats).
notes: Integer division/modulo sign class. Only std.mod calls with comptime arguments (or JS calls) change; the `%` operator and runtime GPU std.mod are untouched. The ported/auto/mod tests use runtime arguments and hard-coded expectations, so they do not see it.

title: i32() cast saturates instead of wrapping
description: CPU/comptime i32(v) clamps the truncated value to the i32 range instead of "v | 0" wrap-around (e.g. i32(10000000000) becomes 2147483647 instead of 1410065408).
notes: u32/i32 overflow semantics. Only comptime/CPU-evaluated casts of out-of-range values are affected.

title: for-of over std.range runs one extra iteration
description: Generated loop header uses "<=" instead of "<" for non-unrolled `for (const i of std.range(...))` loops with positive step.
notes: Off-by-one in generated code. No ex13/investigation suite uses non-unrolled std.range loops (checked by grep), so only docs examples reach it.

title: Guarded compute pipeline guard uses ">" instead of ">="
description: The WGSL bounds guard of createGuardedComputePipeline becomes `any(in.id > sizeUniform)`: one extra thread per dimension executes the callback.
notes: Comparison swapped (< vs <=). Caught by dispatch's atomic counter on any backend; harness-based suites that dispatchThreads() with one thread are unaffected.

title: dispatchThreads computes workgroup count with floor instead of ceil
description: dispatchWorkgroups(floor(threads / workgroupSize)): sizes not divisible by the workgroup size lose the last partial workgroup; sizes smaller than the workgroup dispatch nothing.
notes: Dispatch-size class (cf. indirect dispatch size). dispatch test with 7 threads on a 256-wide group dispatches 0 groups.

title: Workgroup barrier removed from the prefix-scan up-sweep
description: The std.workgroupBarrier() at the top of each up-sweep iteration is deleted; threads read workgroupMemory entries other threads have not yet written.
notes: A race: deterministic wrong sums on emulators that run invocations sequentially/coroutine-style (Lavapipe, SwiftShader), possibly passing on lock-step hardware. @typegpu/sort has no unit tests in the repo and no docs snapshot covers the scan shaders.

title: Workgroup barrier removed between down-sweep and the final read
description: Deleted std.workgroupBarrier() after downsweep(localIdx): scannedSum is read before every invocation finished its down-sweep writes.
notes: Misplaced/missing barrier class; only the final write-back depends on the race, so results are subtler than M34.

title: std.atomicSub emits atomicAdd
description: Copy-paste bug in the atomic op mapping: atomicSub(&a, v) is emitted as atomicAdd(&a, v).
notes: Atomic op mapping class. Only one docs example uses atomicSub; none of the 13 tests or investigation suites does. Mocked docs snapshot contains the call text.

title: rg* texture formats get the wrong bytes-per-texel (default 4)
description: The texel-size regex no longer matches the "rg" prefix: rg8 formats report 4 bytes (should be 2), rg32 formats 4 (should be 8). texture.write() computes the wrong expected size / bytesPerRow.
notes: Texture bytes-per-pixel class. rg16* are unaffected (16 bits x 2 = 4 by luck). Surfaces as a thrown size-mismatch error or garbage texels.

title: u32To01F32 drops the lowest mantissa bit
description: Mask 0x007fffff -> 0x007ffffe in the u32 -> [0,1) float conversion shared by every @typegpu/noise generator: all random floats lose one ulp of resolution.
notes: Subtle 1-ulp numeric change; found by bit-exact comparison against the unmutated run, not by tolerance checks. CPU and GPU change together so prng-cpu-gpu stays consistent.

title: GPU-side hash multiplier differs from the CPU one by one bit
description: In hash() the transpiled (GPU) branch multiplies by 0xac4c1b50 while the CPU branch keeps 0xac4c1b51: seeded GPU sequences diverge from the CPU reference.
notes: Noise/numeric-constant class; CPU-vs-GPU mismatch is checked directly by the prng-cpu-gpu example. Mocked snapshots contain the hash WGSL.

title: srgbToLinear uses gamma 2.2 instead of 2.4
description: The power-curve branch of srgbToLinear uses exponent 2.2 (classic approximation) instead of the sRGB 2.4.
notes: Numeric-constant class in @typegpu/color (no unit tests there). Small colour shifts, visible only with an output hash/pixel comparison.

title: opSmoothUnion blend term loses a factor h
description: smooth-min correction "h * h * k * 1/4" becomes "h * k * 1/4": the blend region is too wide/strong.
notes: SDF constant class. Only the smooth-union blend zone changes (visible near the seam of the two shapes).

title: Bitonic sort default paddingValue 0x7fffffff instead of 0xffffffff
description: Default padding for non-power-of-two arrays is half of u32 range: arrays containing values >= 0x7fffffff sort incorrectly (padding is not the maximum).
notes: Default-value class. Deliberately unreachable by the test inputs (values 0..255), a "test data too narrow" case.

title: std.select emits select(t, f, cond)
description: Generated WGSL swaps the false/true branches of std.select (argument-order bug; inverts the condition).
notes: Runtime GPU path only: select with comptime args is folded by the CPU impl, so the tgsl-parsing-test constants do not see it.

title: CPU .rgb swizzle returns (r, b, g)
description: The 3-length rgba-alias swizzles on the CPU pick components (e0, e2, e1): v.rgb of a CPU/comptime vector is wrong while v.xyz is right.
notes: Swizzle/component mapping class. GPU codegen emits the swizzle text unchanged, so only CPU-evaluated or comptime-folded swizzles change.

title: rotationY4 WGSL sign error
description: The generated WGSL for d.mat4x4f.rotationY / std.rotateY4 flips the signs of the sin terms (rotates the other way); the CPU implementation stays correct.
notes: CPU vs GPU divergence. tgsl-parsing-test folds rotationY with constants (CPU impl), so the broken codegen text is only emitted for runtime angles.

title: std.insertBits emits the base value and the inserted bits swapped
description: Generated WGSL calls insertBits(newbits, e, offset, count) instead of insertBits(e, newbits, offset, count).
notes: Bit-op argument order. No CPU implementation and zero mocked-test mentions of insertBits (grep over unit tests and docs snapshots): a GPU-only catch candidate.

title: std.firstLeadingBit emits firstTrailingBit
description: Copy-paste bug: firstLeadingBit(x) is emitted as firstTrailingBit(x).
notes: Equal for single-bit inputs, different for any value with several bits set. No mocked test mentions firstLeadingBit; no CPU implementation.

title: std.countTrailingZeros emits firstTrailingBit
description: Copy-paste bug: countTrailingZeros(x) is emitted as firstTrailingBit(x). The two agree for every x != 0 and differ only at x == 0 (32 vs -1/0xFFFFFFFF).
notes: Extremely subtle: only the zero input exposes it (the suites include 0 in their edge lists). No CPU impl; zero mocked-test mentions of countTrailingZeros.

title: std.dot4U8Packed emits dot4I8Packed
description: Copy-paste bug: unsigned packed dot product is emitted as the signed variant: bytes >= 128 are treated as negative.
notes: Equal whenever every packed byte is < 128. Needs the dot4*Packed extension (WGSL language feature) on the backend. No mocked-test mentions.

title: std.trunc emits floor
description: Copy-paste bug: trunc(x) is emitted as floor(x): differs for negative non-integers (round toward -inf instead of 0).
notes: No CPU implementation and zero mocked-test mentions of trunc; vector-fns/specs.ts and ported/semantics exercise it on the GPU.
